skill.name: dealport
skill.description: Use when the user wants to find, size, research, score, or contact off-market US small and mid-sized businesses (28M+ private companies), commercial buildings, or the human principals behind them; match a CSV of company names or domains; monitor target companies in a Project; or request double-opt-in owner introductions through Avery.
skill.summary: Size US private company markets, research company and property records, and track acquisition targets in Dealport.
skill.author: dealport-hq

security_audit.summary: Most backtick matches are Markdown formatting, but the skill also directs agents to run an unpinned CLI and use a remote MCP service. The workflow can upload account lists, persist scoring notes, and configure outbound webhooks without clearly requiring user approval. No evidence was found of instructions to manipulate the audit or deliberately exfiltrate data.

remediation.issue: The CLI examples execute an unpinned package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Use an approved MCP connection or a verified, pinned CLI release. Require user approval before installing a package or adding a remote server.

remediation.issue: The login example puts the API key in a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Document a secret-entry flow that keeps the key out of command arguments, shell history, and chat.

remediation.issue: CSV matching does not require approval for the external transfer.
remediation.suggestion: Show the receiving workspace and proposed columns before upload. Send only approved company names or domains.

remediation.issue: Ranking automatically writes scores and rationale to a Dealport Project.
remediation.suggestion: Keep rankings read-only by default. Ask the user to approve the destination Project and the exact fields before saving.

remediation.issue: Webhook creation, activation, and testing lack an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for webhook creation, activation, and tests. Verify destination ownership and restrict test payloads and event fields to approved data.

remediation.issue: Budget approval is not consistent across paid lookups and recurring monitoring.
remediation.suggestion: Show the maximum cost and any recurring charges before starting. Keep the separate, target-specific confirmation for Avery outreach and introductions.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory External Writeback of Rankings
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires Dealport writeback whenever it ranks companies. A read-only evaluation request could therefore persist internal scores and rationale in a workspace Project.

semantic_findings.title: Webhook Delivery Without Destination Approval

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill lists webhook creation, toggling, and testing but requires confirmation only for deletion. It does not document destination verification or payload review.

content.user_title: Research Private Companies and Acquisition Targets
content.value_statement: Researching private companies often means checking fragmented filings, company websites, and account lists. Dealport previews matching markets, retrieves cited records, and helps teams rank and monitor targets.
actual_capabilities: Preview the number of matching US companies and review five sample companies before opening paid records.
Retrieve cited company and building records, read company website pages, and distinguish filed, observed, and estimated facts.
Match up to 250 company names or domains from a CSV against Dealport records.
Score companies against a Playbook, record the rationale in a Project, and review weekly changes for watched companies.
Check workspace exclusions and look up available verified business owner contact details.
Request double-opt-in owner introductions through Avery, Dealport's AI outreach specialist, after explicit human confirmation.
limitations: Live actions require an authenticated Dealport MCP connection or the Dealport CLI, which requires Node 20 or newer.
CSV matching is limited to 250 rows per request. The documented building search and building owner lookup cover NYC.
Record retrieval, some research, owner contact hits, and recurring monitoring may use account balance. Workspace spend limits may stop requests.
Owner contact details are not always available. Avery cannot guarantee replies or introductions.

use_cases.title: Size an Acquisition Market
use_cases.description: Estimate how many independent companies match an industry, state, and employee threshold before paying for detailed records.

use_cases.title: Match an Existing Account List
use_cases.description: Match approved company names or domains to Dealport records and flag ambiguous or unmatched rows for review.

use_cases.title: Screen New York City Buildings
use_cases.description: Search commercial or multifamily buildings by borough, unit count, and loan maturity. Review the cited records before requesting owner research.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview independent HVAC contractors in Ohio with at least 15 employees. Show the matching count and five samples. Do not open paid records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Check whether a market is large enough to research.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Company Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the expected cost before retrieving the cited record for this company ID. Label revenue, headcount, and ownership as filed, observed, or estimated.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Verify the basis for key company facts.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a CSV Match
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided CSV and propose up to 250 company names or domains for matching. Wait for approval before sending the selected columns to Dealport.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review the fields intended for an external match.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Candidates for a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply our Playbook to approved candidate records. Provide a score, verdict, rationale, and citation for each company. Ask before saving scores or enabling paid monitoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Create an auditable shortlist before changing the workspace.

output_examples.input: Preview the Ohio HVAC market without opening paid records.
output: Illustrative result: 84 companies match the selected filters.
The preview returns five samples for review. No paid records were opened.

output_examples.input: Score a candidate but do not write to the Project.
output: A state filing supports the license status. The company website describes commercial services.
Headcount is an estimate. No score was saved to Dealport.

best_practices: Use a free preview and agree on a spending limit before requesting paid records or recurring monitoring.
Review citations and distinguish filed facts, observed facts, and estimates when ranking targets.
Confirm the destination and required fields before sharing CSV files, saving notes, or enabling webhooks.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated revenue or headcount as verified facts.
Uploading unrelated CRM fields or assuming a ranking request authorizes saving notes to a Project.
Requesting outreach or accepting a paid introduction without explicit approval of the company, person, and cost.

faq.question: How do I connect Dealport?
faq.answer: Use an authenticated Dealport MCP connection or the Dealport CLI with Node 20 or later. Keep API keys out of chat.

faq.question: Is market sizing free?
faq.answer: The documented market preview is free. Detailed records, some live website reads, and other follow-up actions can incur charges.

faq.question: Can I match a CSV of companies?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports matching up to 250 names or domains per request. Approve the selected columns before sending them to Dealport.

faq.question: What do the evidence labels mean?
faq.answer: Filed facts come from filings. Observed facts come from sources such as company websites. Estimates should not be treated as verified figures.

faq.question: Can I monitor companies after ranking them?
faq.answer: Yes. A Dealport Project can track companies and show weekly changes. Monitoring is priced per company per month.

faq.question: When can Avery contact an owner?
faq.answer: Avery requires explicit human confirmation of the company, the person, and the USD cost before sending outreach or accepting an introduction.
